source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: No early-papyrus witness preserves Matthew 1 within the 2nd-3rd c. CE corpus for these target verses; primary witnesses are the 4th c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference (where variants are documented)
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997; Luz Hermeneia 2001-2007; France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1993-1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Brown Birth of the Messiah 1993; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form (with breathings and accents) as transmitted via SBLGNT (which is essentially the consensus modern critical text closely tracking Vaticanus + Sinaiticus). Variant readings where Vaticanus and Sinaiticus diverge — or where an early papyrus preserves a different reading — are documented in the per-verse `notes` field. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua (no word divisions, no punctuation, no breathings or accents); the SBLGNT polytonic-with-spaces is the modern critical reconstruction. Sacred names (nomina sacra) — ΙΗΣΟΥΣ, ΧΡΙΣΤΟΣ, ΚΥΡΙΟΣ, ΘΕΟΣ, ΠΝΕΥΜΑ, ΥΙΟΣ, ΠΑΤΗΡ — appear in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus as scribal abbreviations (e.g., ΙΣ, ΧΣ, ΚΣ, ΘΣ, ΠΝΑ, ΥΣ, ΠΗΡ) with an overbar; this paleographic convention is not reproduced in the modern critical text.

verses.text: Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ.
verses.translit: Biblos geneseōs Iēsou christou huiou Dauid huiou Abraam.
verses.notes: MAJOR FRAMING — the genealogical incipit. The phrase *biblos geneseōs* deliberately echoes Gen 2:4 LXX (αὕτη ἡ βίβλος γενέσεως οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς) and Gen 5:1 LXX (αὕτη ἡ βίβλος γενέσεως ἀνθρώπων), framing the entire genealogy as a new creation / new humanity narrative. The double *huiou* link (son of David / son of Abraham) signals the dual royal-Davidic + covenantal-Abrahamic claim. cf. Brown 1993 Birth of the Messiah; Davies-Allison ICC 1.149-160; France NICNT 25-31.

verses.text: Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Abraam egennēsen ton Isaak, Isaak de egennēsen ton Iakōb, Iakōb de egennēsen ton Ioudan kai tous adelphous autou,
verses.notes: The first triad of the patriarchal series. *egennēsen* ("begat") repeats formulaically through the genealogy — a deliberate stylistic device echoing the LXX-genealogy form (Gen 5; Gen 11; 1 Chr 1-3). The mention of Judah's brothers (τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ) is unique to Matthew (Luke's parallel omits it), signaling the twelve-tribes frame.

verses.text: Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζαρὰ ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀράμ,
verses.translit: Ioudas de egennēsen ton Phares kai ton Zara ek tēs Thamar, Phares de egennēsen ton Hesrōm, Hesrōm de egennēsen ton Aram,
verses.notes: FIRST OF FOUR WOMEN — Tamar (Thamar). The inclusion of four Hebrew Bible women (Tamar v.3, Rahab v.5, Ruth v.5, 'wife of Uriah' v.6) plus Mary (v.16) is a deliberate Matthean structural device. cf. Brown 1993 Birth of the Messiah 71-74; Levine-Brettler JANT note ad loc. The four women all have irregular sexual circumstances (Tamar's Judah; Rahab the Canaanite prostitute; Ruth the Moabite; Bathsheba taken by David); this prepares the Matthean defense of Mary's irregular conception.

verses.text: Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών,
verses.translit: Aram de egennēsen ton Aminadab, Aminadab de egennēsen ton Naassōn, Naassōn de egennēsen ton Salmōn,
verses.notes: The pre-monarchic generations. Aminadab and Naasson are tribal leaders of Judah at the exodus period (Num 1:7; 2:3); Salmon is the link into the Rahab/Boaz line.

verses.text: Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βοὲς ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βοὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί,
verses.translit: Salmōn de egennēsen ton Boes ek tēs Rhachab, Boes de egennēsen ton Iōbēd ek tēs Rhouth, Iōbēd de egennēsen ton Iessai,
verses.notes: SECOND AND THIRD WOMEN — Rahab (Rhachab) and Ruth (Rhouth). Rahab the Canaanite prostitute (Josh 2; 6) appears here as ancestor of David; this is a uniquely Matthean tradition not attested in Hebrew Bible chronology (the canonical HB does not name Rahab as Salmon's wife). Ruth the Moabite (the book of Ruth) is a non-Israelite ancestor. Variant: SBLGNT/NA28 read Βοές (Boes); some witnesses read Βόοζ (Booz) following LXX Ruth. Vaticanus reads Βοες; Sinaiticus reads Βοος.

verses.text: Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα. Δαυὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου,
verses.translit: Iessai de egennēsen ton Dauid ton basilea. Dauid de egennēsen ton Solomōna ek tēs tou Ouriou,
verses.notes: FOURTH WOMAN — periphrastically named as "the (wife) of Uriah" (τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου), not as Bathsheba. The naming-by-husband foregrounds the adultery (2 Sam 11) rather than the woman's identity. The royal title βασιλέα (king) is appended to David — marking the structural mid-point of the genealogy from Abraham → David → exile → Christ (cf. v. 17). Davies-Allison ICC 1.176-178; Brown 1993 73-74.

verses.text: Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ,
verses.translit: Solomōn de egennēsen ton Rhoboam, Rhoboam de egennēsen ton Abia, Abia de egennēsen ton Asaph,
verses.notes: Variant: NA28/SBLGNT read Ἀσάφ (Asaph — the psalmist's name, an apparent scribal error/conflation) where the Hebrew Bible has Asa (אסא, the Judahite king, 1 Kgs 15:8-24). Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + most early witnesses read Ἀσάφ. THGNT preserves Asaph. Some later witnesses correct to Asa. This is one of the documented Matthean genealogical irregularities.

verses.text: Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν,
verses.translit: Asaph de egennēsen ton Iōsaphat, Iōsaphat de egennēsen ton Iōram, Iōram de egennēsen ton Ozian,
verses.notes: Three Judahite kings omitted between Joram and Uzziah (Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah — 2 Kgs 8-14) to achieve the 14-14-14 structural symmetry announced in v.17. Davies-Allison ICC 1.174; France NICNT 33.

verses.text: Ὀζίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ, Ἰωαθὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχάζ, Ἀχὰζ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑζεκίαν,
verses.translit: Ozias de egennēsen ton Iōatham, Iōatham de egennēsen ton Achaz, Achaz de egennēsen ton Hezekian,
verses.notes: The late-monarchic Judahite kings. Ahaz is the addressee of the Isa 7:14 oracle that will be cited at Mt 1:23. Hezekiah is the deliverer-king of 2 Kgs 18-20 / Isa 36-39.

verses.text: Ἑζεκίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μανασσῆ, Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσίαν,
verses.translit: Hezekias de egennēsen ton Manassē, Manassēs de egennēsen ton Amōs, Amōs de egennēsen ton Iōsian,
verses.notes: Variant: NA28/SBLGNT read Ἀμώς (Amos — the prophet's name, again an apparent scribal conflation) where the Hebrew Bible has Amon (אמון, the Judahite king, 2 Kgs 21:18-26). Vaticanus + Sinaiticus read Ἀμώς. Some later witnesses correct to Ἀμών. Paired with the v.7 Asaph/Asa variant — both are prophet-for-king substitutions.

verses.text: Ἰωσίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος.
verses.translit: Iōsias de egennēsen ton Iechonian kai tous adelphous autou epi tēs metoikesias Babylōnos.
verses.notes: STRUCTURAL HINGE — the Babylonian exile (μετοικεσία Βαβυλῶνος) marks the second 14-generation block-break. Note: Josiah's actual son was Jehoiakim, whose son was Jeconiah (1 Chr 3:15-16); Matthew has telescoped a generation to maintain the 14-14-14 schema. Davies-Allison ICC 1.184.

verses.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβαβέλ,
verses.translit: Meta de tēn metoikesian Babylōnos Iechonias egennēsen ton Salathiēl, Salathiēl de egennēsen ton Zorobabel,
verses.notes: The post-exilic restoration line. Zerubbabel (Hag 1:1, 2:23; Zech 4) is the messianic-prefigurement figure of the post-exilic period; the genealogy now passes into largely obscure names (the Davidic line post-Zerubbabel is poorly attested in HB sources).

verses.text: Ζοροβαβὲλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ, Ἀβιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιακίμ, Ἐλιακὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀζώρ,
verses.translit: Zorobabel de egennēsen ton Abioud, Abioud de egennēsen ton Eliakim, Eliakim de egennēsen ton Azōr,
verses.notes: Names not attested in Hebrew Bible Davidic genealogy (1 Chr 3); Matthew's source for these post-exilic generations is unknown — possibly a now-lost family-genealogy tradition, possibly Matthean construction. Luke's parallel genealogy (Luke 3:23-38) has a completely different post-Zerubbabel list.

verses.text: Ἀζὼρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαδώκ, Σαδὼκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχίμ, Ἀχὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιούδ,
verses.translit: Azōr de egennēsen ton Sadōk, Sadōk de egennēsen ton Achim, Achim de egennēsen ton Elioud,
verses.notes: Continuation of the otherwise-unattested post-exilic Davidic line. Sadōk shares the name of the high-priestly line (Zadok) — possibly significant for a priestly-Davidic conflation, possibly coincidence.

verses.text: Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ματθάν, Ματθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ,
verses.translit: Elioud de egennēsen ton Eleazar, Eleazar de egennēsen ton Matthan, Matthan de egennēsen ton Iakōb,
verses.notes: The final pre-Joseph generations. The grandfather's name Iakōb deliberately echoes the patriarch Jacob (v.2) — closing a structural inclusio at the moment Joseph (= the patriarch Joseph echo) is about to be named.

verses.text: Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός.
verses.translit: Iakōb de egennēsen ton Iōsēph ton andra Marias, ex hēs egennēthē Iēsous ho legomenos christos.
verses.notes: STRUCTURAL CULMINATION — the genealogy breaks its formula at the final link. Instead of *Iōsēph egennēsen ton Iēsoun*, Matthew shifts to a passive (ἐγεννήθη — "was begotten / born") with Mary as the immediate antecedent (ἐξ ἧς — "from whom," feminine relative). This is the deliberate grammatical signal of the virgin conception. Variant readings: a small group of witnesses (Sinaitic Syriac, some OL) read "Joseph, to whom was betrothed the virgin Mary, begat Jesus" — generally regarded as a harmonizing or adoptionist reading and not preferred. The Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + main tradition all preserve the passive *ἐγεννήθη*. cf. Brown 1993 61-64; Davies-Allison ICC 1.183-184. FIFTH WOMAN — Mary, the climactic fifth in the four-women pattern set up at vv.3, 5, 6.

verses.text: Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
verses.translit: Pasai oun hai geneai apo Abraam heōs Dauid geneai dekatessares, kai apo Dauid heōs tēs metoikesias Babylōnos geneai dekatessares, kai apo tēs metoikesias Babylōnos heōs tou christou geneai dekatessares.
verses.notes: MAJOR FRAMING — the 14-14-14 schematization explicitly stated. The number 14 = 2×7 (double perfection) and also the gematria value of דוד (DWD = 4+6+4 = 14) — the latter reading is the standard explanation in modern critical scholarship (Davies-Allison ICC 1.163-165; Brown 1993 74-81; cf. Levine-Brettler JANT). The arithmetic is in tension: counting strictly yields 14+14+13 generations; the Babylon-exile generation may be double-counted, or Jeconiah may be counted twice, to recover 14+14+14. The schematic intent matters more than the arithmetic.

verses.text: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν. μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσήφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
verses.translit: Tou de Iēsou christou hē genesis houtōs ēn. mnēsteutheisēs tēs mētros autou Marias tō Iōsēph, prin ē synelthein autous heurethē en gastri echousa ek pneumatos hagiou.
verses.notes: MAJOR FRAMING — the virgin-birth narrative begins. The conception is attributed *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("from holy spirit" / "out of holy spirit"). The phrase has no article (anarthrous *pneumatos hagiou*) — this is grammatically the standard Matthean idiom and does not in itself signal full Trinitarian theology (which is anachronistic at the 1st-c. textual layer). **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: Raël *The Role of Christ* reads this as the engineered-conception of the chosen one; canon reading: 'engineered by the Elohim using the Mary genome.' **LENS-RISK FLAG for the Editor**: do NOT pre-resolve toward either (a) the Raëlian engineered-conception reading or (b) the orthodox-Christian Trinitarian Holy-Spirit reading. Preserve the textual *ek pneumatos hagiou* with philological discipline. cf. Brown 1993 124-138; Davies-Allison ICC 1.197-201.

verses.text: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν.
verses.translit: Iōsēph de ho anēr autēs, dikaios ōn kai mē thelōn autēn deigmatisai, eboulēthē lathra apolysai autēn.
verses.notes: Joseph's quiet-divorce decision. The adjective *dikaios* ("just/righteous") is loaded — does it mean (a) Joseph is law-observant and obliged to divorce, but compassionately, or (b) Joseph is righteous in the sense of not wanting to expose Mary to shame? Both readings have ancient and modern defenders. Variant: some witnesses read *deigmatisai* (expose to disgrace) vs *paradeigmatisai* (make a public example); the NA28/SBLGNT/Vaticanus reading is *deigmatisai*. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.202-205.

verses.text: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου κατ' ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυίδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου, τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου·
verses.translit: tauta de autou enthymēthentos idou angelos kyriou kat' onar ephanē autō legōn· Iōsēph huios Dauid, mē phobēthēs paralabein Marian tēn gynaika sou, to gar en autē gennēthen ek pneumatos estin hagiou·
verses.notes: DREAM-VISION — the first of Joseph's five dreams in Matthew (1:20, 2:13, 2:19, 2:22; cf. 27:19 Pilate's wife). The angel-of-the-Lord (ἄγγελος κυρίου) idiom is a direct LXX-translation of *malʾakh YHWH* (Hebrew Bible theophany formula). The dream-revelation pattern recalls the patriarch Joseph (Gen 37; 40-41). Note the address *huios Dauid* — Joseph's Davidic line is what legally transmits Davidic descent to Jesus (via adoption, not biological paternity). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the canon reading interprets the dream-angel as Elohim-message-bearer — disavow Sitchin/Anunnaki-engineered pre-resolution; disavow Raëlian-canon engineered-conception pre-resolution; preserve text as theophanic dream-vision.

verses.text: τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: texetai de huion kai kaleseis to onoma autou Iēsoun, autos gar sōsei ton laon autou apo tōn hamartiōn autōn.
verses.notes: NAME-ETYMOLOGY — Iēsous (Hebrew Yēšūaʿ / Yehōšūaʿ) etymologized via *sōsei* (will save) — the Hebrew Yēšūaʿ derives from yšʿ (to save / deliver). The naming-by-angel-before-conception pattern echoes Gen 16:11 (Ishmael), Gen 17:19 (Isaac), Judg 13:3-5 (Samson), Isa 7:14 (Immanuel) — all annunciation-type scenes. *ton laon autou* = his people = Israel (not pre-emptively universalized; the universalization comes only at Mt 28:19). cf. Brown 1993 130-135.

verses.text: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
verses.translit: touto de holon gegonen hina plērōthē to rhēthen hypo kyriou dia tou prophētou legontos·
verses.notes: MATTHEAN FULFILLMENT-FORMULA — the first of Matthew's ~10 *hina plērōthē* ("so that it might be fulfilled") quotations, a signature Matthean device that frames the entire Gospel as the eschatological-fulfillment of Israel's scriptures. The structural pattern: event → fulfillment-formula → scripture-quotation → narrative continues. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.209-213.

verses.text: Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ· ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: Idou hē parthenos en gastri hexei kai texetai huion, kai kalesousin to onoma autou Emmanouēl· ho estin methermēneuomenon Meth' hēmōn ho theos.
verses.notes: MAJOR PHILOLOGICAL CRUX — citation of Isa 7:14. Matthew quotes the **LXX** reading *parthenos* (virgin) — the Hebrew Bible original reads *ʿalmâ* (young woman of marriageable age; not specifically virgin — Hebrew *bětûlâ* would specify virginity). The LXX-vs-Hebrew divergence is the foundational text-critical dispute of the virgin-birth narrative. cf. Brown 1993 145-150; Davies-Allison ICC 1.213-216; Levine-Brettler JANT note ad loc. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve the LXX-Hebrew divergence as a documented philological dispute — do NOT resolve toward either Christian (parthenos-=-virgin definitively) or Jewish (ʿalmâ-=-young-woman definitively) reading; the Editor must present both. The name *Immanouēl* (= *ʿimmānū ʾēl*, "with us is God / El") is glossed by Matthew with the Greek calque *Meth' hēmōn ho theos*. **The Raëlian-canon engineered-conception reading would interpret 'with us is God' as 'with us is the Elohim representative' — flag for Editor disavowal, preserve text.**

verses.text: ἐγερθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν αὐτῷ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου καὶ παρέλαβεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: egertheis de ho Iōsēph apo tou hypnou epoiēsen hōs prosetaxen autō ho angelos kyriou kai parelaben tēn gynaika autou·
verses.notes: The Joseph-obedience report. The verb *parelaben* (took to himself) echoes the v.20 angelic command *paralabein* — the obedience is literal, formulaic. The pattern (command → obedience) recurs at Mt 2:13-14, 2:19-21, 2:22-23.

verses.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: kai ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken huion· kai ekalesen to onoma autou Iēsoun.
verses.notes: *ouk eginōsken* — the LXX-idiomatic euphemism for sexual relations (cf. Gen 4:1 LXX, *Adam egnō Heuan*). The *heōs hou* (until) construction has been the locus of major theological dispute: Catholic/Orthodox tradition (perpetual virginity of Mary) reads it as not implying post-partum relations; Protestant tradition typically reads it as implying that Joseph and Mary did consummate after Jesus's birth (cf. Mt 12:46-47 brothers of Jesus). Variant: some later Byzantine witnesses add *ton prōtotokon* (the firstborn) — absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + NA28/SBLGNT; the longer reading is a harmonization with Luke 2:7. cf. Davies-Allison ICC 1.219-220; Brown 1993 132.
